notes.title: Weekly Update 29 - More Shaders and Future Balancing
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/7649dab7aeae5870f49e3e63dc1898a90265c602.png[/img][h1]Hey everyone![/h1]
Last week we made good progress on the tiling system, did some further work on the shader for rivers and waterfalls, and started working on a procedural shader for tree barks (the title image is one of our shader creations). 

We are experimenting with procedural bark for a couple of reasons: Having a shader instead of a texture will mean that we can implement a variety of moss or weather conditions for the trees based on their location; it will mean that we should be able to have different bark on the same asset based on location; and it will remove a resolution limit on larger assets. The latter is most notable currently with the polynesian palm trees. While we love their scale in the game and their presence in the jungle, the bark looks quite pixelated up close. Additionally, when different levels of LOD load in, we are working to make the transitions smoother. 

Considering all of these are still works in progress and rather technical, we want to use this blog to also talk about some higher level considerations of ours. In particular, we want to discuss the depth and balancing of our production chains. At the moment, the amount of buildings we have is the minimum we considered to be viable to make the game work when we planned it out at the start of the project. Production chains are rather limited, and most of the early buildings are rather expensive while also giving you a really high rate of return. 

When John and I have been playing the game as a team, we tried to specialise on certain aspects (exploration vs base building), which has made us realise how few decisions the base builder has to make in the early game before their economy starts to bring in money. Considering the starting capital of 2k and the cost of e.g. a farm and seeds, it generally isn’t possible to place more than one field before you run out of money - which is obviously not a great way to start the game.

With that in mind, we are planning to adjust the balancing of the early game (wooden tier) to being much cheaper while also having less of a payoff. This should also mean that you need more space and more villagers to produce goods compared to the latter tier production facilities, which will give a nice incentive to upgrade and will mean that villages will have to grow quickly from the very beginning.

Until next week!

notes.title: Weekly Update 26 - Building Attacks

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/6cd016f51d70ad0c71455e63850d7ad620695611.png[/img][h1]Hey everyone![/h1]
Last week has been largely focused on continuing work on building attacks and bug fixes, but I am also going to talk a little bit about the current state of our animations.

Starting with the bug fixes, we found a decent number of bugs in the latest version, which were luckily pretty easy to fix (e.g. pirates not attacking on Spike Ridge, water not drowning the player on Spike Ridge, etc). As a result, we will be uploading another update tomorrow evening (after some more testing), which will include the aforementioned fixes as well as the new pirate mechanics.

Secondly, work on the building attacks has progressed nicely. At the moment, pirates will attack buildings if they get close to them and there are no soldiers or villagers nearby. If soldiers or villagers are nearby, they will prioritise shooting them first, then turn to the buildings.

Building attacks are now based on the soldier/pirate getting close to the building (closer than they would come to shoot), and then each attack removes some health from the building. The range and damage will obviously be adjustable for additional units in the future, but the general setup will likely remain the same. 

One pretty apparent gap at the moment is our lack of animations for this. When finished, we want the pirates to throw a torch at the building for the attack animation, and for buildings to get gradually damaged to show their hitpoints. However, animations take quite a bit of time to make, and considering how close we are to implementing the new villager model, we want to focus on making the animations for the new model, rather than having to make the animations twice. 

Under normal circumstances, we would simply hold off on releasing the new mechanic until we have the animation ready. However, I consider the building attack to be a very important part of my upgrade of the pirates. Therefore, adding it, even without an animation, gives players a chance to experience pirate attacks as they are intended. Let us know your thoughts on this, however - we are always happy to receive feedback on our approach.

Until next week!

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/c088049c6704d4b7f89a948736da846111ba6485.png[/img]
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]

First of all, thank you to everyone who gave us feedback on last week’s update, it seems that the new look of the ocean was particularly attractive to many! With that in mind, I have already worked on a shader for our foliage, which will include wind movement - and John has also started looking into a way to decrease the harsh shadow changes in the tree canopies.

Regarding the attacks against buildings, those of you who have played the game against other players (not too many competitive players around though!) know that soldiers currently attack buildings by only standing in front of the door. If they haven’t been killed by an opponent after 30 seconds, the building gets destroyed. 

This approach was largely a result of us thinking about how to simplify the way a building would get destroyed by marauders in the real world (most likely by setting fire to it with a torch), which we wanted to emulate by them having to survive in close proximity to the building for a little while. The desire for a “realistic” approach was somewhat driven by the first person perspective of the game, and trying to avoid anything that would break immersion too badly (and who doesn’t get immersed in 30 seconds of animation-less waiting?).

With the RTS update on the horizon and a desire to improve the behaviour of pirates, we have now decided to go more in the direction of a traditional RTS: In the past week, I added hitpoints to buildings, which can be removed by attacks by multiple enemy units, and villagers will repair damaged buildings (see image above). As a result, it will be possible to have more than one soldier (or pirate) attacking a building, and more attackers will destroy the building quicker.

In the coming week(s), we will be working on implementing this as a default behaviour for pirates as they come across your settlements.

Until next week!

[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]
Last week has been largely dedicated to finally implementing the Stone Mason, as well as testing the new team play part of the game.

Firstly, implementing the Stone Mason and villagers collecting Stone from boulders has opened up a big additional feature for maps: The possibility for us to close off certain valleys and walkways with rocks, which can be cleared by the players over the course of the game. This will allow us to more effectively separate players in the early game, delay access to certain areas, and help players funnel their opponents in more creative ways.

Secondly, as we mentioned in last week’s update, we have been trying to test the new teamplay. While this has led to a ton of straightforward fixes and improvements (having changed added a lot of functions led to many new issues), we also wanted to test what it feels like to play the game together, for balancing and gameplay concerns. 

One of the outcomes of this, for example, was a new chest that has been placed next to the Port. Unlike normal chests, this one does not disappear when everything is taken out, and players on the same team can use it to quickly exchange goods with each other when needed. 

Another outcome was a change to the movement of players: With one player being more focused on exploration on the new map, we realised that it can feel quite rewarding to find your way up onto a mountain to scout the terrain ahead of you - but with players being able to just stand on the side of a cliff, the feeling of risk and accomplishment was somewhat reduced. As a result, we have implemented a new sliding mechanic, which makes scaling mountains more difficult and more dangerous - but will hopefully lead to better immersion and more enjoyable scouting!

Until next week!

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/f5ee00073a660bbd4128d1b58e3bb12e9fca8738.png[/img]
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]
Last week has been a little busy in our day jobs, but we managed to do quite a bit on the game nonetheless:

First of all, I managed to create a team victory condition, so people playing together will now share benefits, such as the unlock of their seed market, as well as winning the game. Considering this required quite a few adjustments of the underlying system, I also got around to creating a new victory condition: Artefact mode. In artefact mode, we will have a single, heavily defended chest on the map, and whoever manages to get to it first, wins. This should change competitive gameplay to something more militaristic, but it should also allow coop play (and singleplayer) to have a more specific goal than simply making money (without the time constraint that comes with a human opponent). 

Secondly, we also managed to do a decent amount of testing of the latest changes to soldiers and pirates, and have addressed a few of the more specific bugs as they came up. We are pretty confident that the new system will work very robustly by the time we patch the game.

Finally, I had to address a multiplayer bug that randomly started happening on the test branch, which prevented players from starting the game at certain times. John has also been continuing his work on the performance improvements for the plants, so while we aren't fully happy with the current states of the plants, we are seeing much smoother gameplay across most systems. This will carry across when we improve the trees and plants so they are built off the same performance principles. 

Until next week!

notes.title: Weekly Update 19 - Rudimentary Team Play
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/52e3029aedf885d758b5f4be975321b87964a063.png[/img]
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]
Last week, I joked that there had been a dip in quality from John’s hijack of the weekly update - judging from the approval our respective posts received, I may have to concede that art is more appealing than function, and John may get to do another update in the future ;).

Without further ado, let’s get into the changes we made this week:

[h3]Unexpected team play[/h3]
While team play was originally lower on our list of priorities, I decided to take a quick look into making teamplay work, and I got surprisingly far. At this point, players can choose their teams at the start of the game, and soldiers within the same team won’t shoot each other. Further, players within the same team can set up movement of goods between their warehouses, allowing them to support each other with resources when needed. Once I add a joint victory condition to the mix, we will be able to upload this for some basic 2v2 gameplay, as well as a new coop map we are working on. Stay tuned.

[h3]Further soldier updates[/h3]
Since the patch, we have already worked on improving the soldiers further: With our overall goal of strategic combat in mind, we wanted to A) make it possible to gain a combat advantage through assessing the environment correctly in the moment, and B) make it possible to gain a combat advantage through setting your long term logistics up in the right way.

To achieve point A, we have already added a damage bonus for units on high ground (this meant that we had to implement health bars as well), so placing units along the hill of a choke point will actually give a big advantage to their effectiveness. The inclusion of health bars means that units (and the player) won’t necessarily die from a single shot, and that food also takes the role of healing units/the player. Units continue to eat 1 food per minute and heal/take damage depending on whether the food is available. Players can heal by using food that is in their inventory.

To achieve point B, we made soldier accuracy scale with the distance from their barracks. If your barracks are well placed, and your soldiers fight close to them, their accuracy will be highest, and they should have a distinct advantage over their opponents. Order your soldiers to track half-way across the map and be miles away from their barracks, and their accuracy will suffer. As a result, you will have to create forward bases for successful (and effective) attacks, which will require you to provide food and protection to these outposts as well.

[h3]Unexpected performance update[/h3]
Finally, John unexpectedly got around to making some improvements to the foliage this week, which ended up drastically improving performance. From what we can tell from our limited tests so far, we are looking at approximately 40% higher frame rates, which should really help some of the people with slower computers. Of course we will continue to work on performance throughout, but this was an unscheduled improvement we are very pleased with.

We will keep you updated on the developments, and as always, are looking forward to your feedback about the game and our plans!

Until next week!

notes.title: Weekly Update 18 - Soldier and Pirate Improvements
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/7ca1bde857092104442fe824b98aa5538ed4eb3b.png[/img]
[h1]Hey everyone![/h1]
After last week’s unfortunate dip in update quality, I am happy to report that John is busy working on the villager bodies, and I am back in charge of writing the update.

As briefly mentioned by John, last week saw the release of a patch just ahead of the blog, and a second smaller patch to fix some MacOS issues the day after. The patch included the Quest System (which you can check in the new Tutorial), the Localisation System (which you can’t see yet), and the first parts of the new soldier/pirate behaviour. Considering we wrote about the first two before, I’ll focus on the soldier behaviour today. In the process of writing this, I got a little carried away, so consider this part 1 of 2!

[h3]Soldier behaviour before:[/h3]
Those of you who have played the game know that the behaviour of the soldiers and pirates used to be a bit of a weak point of the game: Pirates across the island were stationary, and would shoot you when you got into view (mind you that they had eyes in the backs of their head and would “look” through shrubbery). Pirates in attack waves and your soldiers were a little better, insofar as they at least had a target to move towards when they weren’t shooting.

[h3]Soldier behaviour now:[/h3]
At this point, we have entirely revamped the soldier/pirate behaviour. Most importantly, soldiers/pirates now have a field of view toward their front. If you approach them from behind, they won’t be able to see you, unless you make a lot of noise. Noise is dependent on how you move (crouching makes the least noise, running makes the most noise), what you move through (avoiding shrubbery is your best bet to not make noise), and how you act (shooting or cutting down trees makes noise). 

If one of the soldiers/pirates hears a noise, they will go to investigate. Depending on how close and how loud the noise was, they may lose interest sooner or later - but if they see you, they will start shooting. If you manage to escape, they will pursue you up to the last location where they saw you. Visibility is blocked by trees and (partially, to different extents) by shrubbery, so if you are crouching or not moving at all, foliage becomes your friend. Once the pirates have not seen or heard you for a while, they will return to their original location. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/c757478799566ae1bef73887033d01a4fd092b46.jpg[/img]
(As you can see in this sketch, trees will block vision, shrubbery will partially block vision, with multiple bushes giving you full cover, and noises will be investigated only if they are loud enough)

Overall, this has already made the world a lot more organic and interesting. Fighting in the middle of the jungle can become a lot more dangerous, as pirates from a wide area can hear you exchange gunshots with a solitary pirate and come to his aid. If you find a solitary pirate close to your base or soldiers, you can now bait them into walking right into an ambush - simply get their attention and stay ahead of them.

We will dedicate the next weekly update to telling you more about the soldier behaviour, so you have something to look forward to ;).

Until next week!

notes.title: Weekly Update 17 - Toward a New Villager
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/98d097e1129716f5ecb9cef6e2db5b2129982a27.jpg[/img][h1]Hey everyone![/h1]
I (John) am hijacking the blog this week, You can hear more about the marvellous adventures of Phil next week. We have a lot to cover. 

As you can see by this week's blog cover photo, We have an update for the character model. I have put a few of the developments next to one another for comparison below, showing how they have evolved as we have gone along. 

When Phil dragged me into this project, telling me I was going to be responsible for the artwork, we really didn’t know what that entailed. As I had no idea how blender worked and was making our initial building prototypes in Sketchup, we set the bar as low as we thought would still work for immersion - and intended to make an internally consistent art style which I was going to be able to achieve. 

Problem was, I really started to enjoy Blender and the more I learnt about the software, the more I wanted to push myself. So even though we started with a low poly art style in mind, and created the first bunch of assets that way - we soon realised I was going to be able to do more. This brings about a couple of issues such as needing to upscale all of the existing artwork (which has been happening steadily with still a long way to go) and trying to determine where we were going to draw the line in the sand. If we have some art work modelled to a high standard, it will contrast against lower standard pieces and the inconsistency can result in a muddled art style. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/e6f1487b5f8183bb15252b79807bdd895964511a.jpg[/img]

We decided one approach to defining this limitation for our artwork, was to model what I thought to be the hardest element first, to a limit we were comfortable with - then bring everything else up to that level. Which is why we focused on the character first as people can be problematic. Hence the nightmare fuel in the progression photos - I have needed to upskill and learn proportion and better representation of human form (though I think the nightmare fuel one would make a good mutant villain ;) ). We have settled on the design we like and I am going to work on retopologizing the high poly sculpt (As seen in the topmost image), and then texturing it, putting it onto a new rig and animating it. Then we will drop it in the game and replace the villagers. 

Once that is done - we can work on a pirate model and then start iterating through different models for the pirates and variety for the villagers. Let us know what you think! Among that series of improvements, I shall also be bringing the other art up to this level.

We wanted a strong looking, wise but kind character to begin with and have focused on a strong nose and brow with kindly, aged eyes. We will iterate hairstyles (and hats for professions) to add variety to this villager before I can add further models. 

We have also just uploaded the latest patch which includes the long awaited soldier improvements. They will now pursue you if they hear you (running is louder than crouching), and they need to actually see you in order to shoot at you. As a result of them investigating sound, the middle has also become a lot more deadly as we have found out in testing ;).

Until next week!

notes.title: Weekly Update 15 - Happy New Year!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/e920ffb37fe3ce0f4e405c71c539e9659822cb98.png[/img]
[h1]Hi everyone![/h1]
First off: Happy new year! I hope that everyone’s year will be the best one yet.

Despite a few disruptions last week, John and I have been able to make some good progress. John worked on the new map as promised, and he also updated the medium house to have a little more detail and look less flat. 

In addition to the ongoing work on the Tutorial, I have also been able to refactor and update the code of the processing buildings (Mill, Bakery, Smelter, etc), to make it more robust, but most importantly, to make it more flexible for the future. This will mean that we are going to be able to introduce various new industry buildings fairly easily, which we are planning to do some time after the upcoming RTS update. 

In particular, the new update allows us to move away from single production steps (one input, e.g. flour, into one output, e.g. bread), and will allow us to go into more complex steps (e.g. 5 wood and 1 gold bar into 1 advanced furniture and 2 wood chippings). As you can see from that example, we will also be able to create byproducts to the production steps, which should allow us to create a variety of ways to use new manufacturing buildings, and create more choices for the players.

I am expecting that we will be able to finish the update to the Tutorial this week, so look out for the new patch in the coming days.

Until next week!

notes.title: Weekly Update 12 - Tutorial and Localisation
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/c9f1ad12d1d76b676c52c00a39e7c68c82850994.png[/img]
[h1]Hi everyone,[/h1]
First of all, I have continued with work on the pirates, and especially with our decision to aim for 0.8 to be focused around RTS strategy, I have somewhat expanded the scope of my rework to accommodate that. 

Secondly, we have been trying to update the Tutorial to explain the game in simpler and more understandable terms. After moving the Tutorial to its own tab (and giving it its own island), we wanted to add a better explanation of how to make money, some combat mechanics, and some exploration. Unfortunately, the current form of the Tutorial was created in a 3 day sprint just ahead of release, and as such, the scalability is lacking. We decided to not add any more tech debt to this, and create a better underlying system for the Tutorial, which will also be helpful as a first iteration of a more generic quest system we want to introduce in a future version.

As a result, I have been working on this new system for much of the last week, and while we were at it, we decided to ready the game for eventual localisation into other languages. While I had created most of the system for that quite some time ago, we were still lacking language banks to draw from, and so the game was defaulting to the text we had manually put in - something we wanted to move away from. John has already started work on creating an english language bank, which will hold all the text in the same place, making editing easier in general. We will continue to update future text (on the Tutorial and otherwise) under this new system. 

Finally, we have started preparing the rocks for the eventual update to the stonecutter/stone mason. While the current rocks have only primitive colliders on them, we have wanted to make them feel a little more organic, so John has been working on creating better LOD’s and custom colliders for this purpose.

Until next week!

notes.title: Weekly Update 11 - Pirates, Satchels, and Dying
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/e1f0e82c92bd3545a705d76ab04359079c06bbad.png[/img]
[h1]Hi everyone,[/h1]
Last week has been pretty productive again! While I initially sat down to fix an issue with the placement of rich mines and chests, we ended up including quite a few additional things in today’s patch:

First of all, we added new ways to die (lucky you): Where you previously could walk on water, your commander will now fall into the water and drown (unless you get out of it again fast enough). Additionally, you can now die from falling, so no more jumping off cliffs to get home faster (unless you want to get home REALLY quickly)! With these additions, we have also implemented some changes to the way the player moves: You will find that walking up hills will slow you down, while walking down hills will speed you up, while also being a little smoother (less hopping).

Beyond the player movement (and death), we also added a new satchel, which will be dropped by pirates instead of chests. The new satchels are smaller, a little less visible, and can only hold Coin. However, satchels will be picked up automatically by the commander, soldiers, or villagers, when walking past them in close proximity. This should hopefully make it a little easier to pick up the Coin dropped by all the pirates your towers have defended you from.

On the topic of pirates, the last patch also added pirate camps in any positions on Spike Ridge that were not taken by players. This should add some variety to the directions the pirates will attack you from, and make defending more interesting. We also added a dropdown menu during the game setup, which you can use to define how much of a threat you want from the pirate waves. You can define the threat to be anywhere from “none” to “extreme”, and we’d love your feedback on how these work for you.

We also made the executive decision to take Opal Reef out of your options for normal play. Opal Reef was our first map for the game, but frankly, it was too small for the gameplay, and we decided to use it for a more dedicated Tutorial instead. You will now find a Tutorial button in the main menu, and we will soon add a second option for a map in the “real” game.

Finally, we also managed to update the skybox! Instead of the “box” with the message at the top (we appreciate all of the jokes that came out of that), we now have a more appealing sky with some moving clouds - again, we’d love to hear what you think.

Last week, I also brought up the topic of “next steps”. We discussed the topic between ourselves as well as with a few of you, and we came up with 4 primary options:

[olist]
[*] We could polish the core gameplay that we currently have further,
[*] We could strengthen the strategy/RTS pillar, by including scouts, maps, and better tactical options,
[*] We could improve the survival/FPS pillar by adding quests and points of interest in the jungle, and 
[*] We could add a “coop” option for multiplayer, so 2 players could build the same Village together.
[/olist]

While we are excited about every single one of these (and they are likely to be the ones we will focus on over the next 6 months), we have decided that the most important one will be the second one, strengthening the strategy/RTS pillar. At the moment, a lot of you already enjoy the exploration and city building game, but admittedly, the RTS gameplay and using soldiers is much weaker than we would like it to be. As a result, we will focus on this for the next 2-3 months, and will try to bring out an RTS update with version 0.8. As always, let us know what you think, and we’d love to hear what you’d like to see as the next priority after that.

Until next week!

notes.title: Weekly Update 10 - Fields and Next Steps
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/f6f54791410d44ed0e8242f27e52a02b93bdf1eb.png[/img]
[h1]Hi everyone,[/h1]
I hope everyone is doing well, and that especially our US players had a good Thanksgiving. As promised, we uploaded the latest patch last week, and in addition to what I already mentioned last week, we included two more changes: 

Firstly, I made some backend changes to the building inventories. The inventories before the patch were very static, i.e. both input and output could store the same amount of goods, and villagers would always try to move goods when there were 10 available. Considering some goods were heavy (and a villager could only carry 5), and some were light (and a villager could carry up to 100), this led to a lot of inefficiencies. I now adjusted the inventories to be more dynamic, and for villagers to move goods according to how much they can carry, so hopefully the logistics should be a little more efficient going forward.

Secondly, we decided to increase the size of the wheat and vegetable fields. We got some feedback from you saying that the fields were too small for what they provided, which we agreed with. We had always intended for fields to be something that would need room to be cleared (forest, etc), and that food would be easier to be created on the edges of the island, so these changes will hopefully be more in line with what we wanted. The sizes are not necessarily final, so please let us know what you think.

With all of the changes for this patch, we have also finally been able to figure out a bug that’s been on our radar for a while: When you placed a productivity building, sometimes fields, construction, etc, would increase speed by about 1000% instead of just 5%. For a while, this was very elusive, but with this patch, it now happens consistently, and I was already able to fix it as a result (new patch to follow shortly).

I have also made good progress in my work on the pirates, so I will hopefully be able to give a more detailed update next week. As we are approaching the finalisation of the pirates, we are also starting to consider where we want to go from here. While there are still many things we want to improve about the existing dynamics (building upgrades, better logistics, trees falling consistently, better seed inventory system, etc), we are finally at a point where the game runs mostly smoothly, and we don't have any game breaking bugs left (feel free to let me know if this isn't the case for you!).

As some of you know, we have a pretty wide range of things on our roadmap, so we will take into account the feedback we have received from you to make a choice about what new mechanic we want to create for version 0.8. We would love to hear your thoughts on this, and will let you know what we have come up with in the next update. 

Until next week!

notes.title: Weekly Update 9 - Multiplayer Saving
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/b006b44b069fbbcaeebe8772f83515fd0fa79c7f.png[/img]
[h1]Hi everyone,[/h1]
Last week has been interesting: We initially set out to work on the pirates, the tutorial, and to do some testing on the Fruit Gatherer. After a week of productive work, we have managed to fix some major bugs, create multiplayer saving and implement auto-saving. I think it is fair to say that we got a little derailed there.

When John and I set out to do our testing in the beginning of the week, we realised that there was a multiplayer bug that stopped us from even starting the game. This was caused by the update to the networking plug-in in the last patch, but since it doesn’t affect all games, we had not been able to catch it on initial testing. So we set out to fix this. 

Once we had succeeded, we started the game again, and managed to play for about 2 hours before my internet disconnected and our game (which was getting really interesting), was officially over. We were understandably frustrated, and John was pushing hard for me to look into multiplayer saving. I had done a lot of foundational work for it when I implemented the save function for the singleplayer, so I decided to briefly investigate how much more work it would take to fully implement; Only two days later, we had a working multiplayer save function (with auto-saving) as well. 

As a result, we were finally able to play on Thursday, and got some insight into the Fruit Gatherer. For one, I really enjoy seeing the villagers walk between banana trees to harvest them. As much as I don’t usually care about “cosmetic” parts of the game, I do always enjoy seeing how much they end up adding to the game. It was also great to see how much more I had to contemplate my food sources based on where I ended up finding banana trees, how many vegetable seeds John had already bought up, and based on the knowledge that there was going to be a limit to how much food I could get in total.

The most interesting part, however, was something I didn’t expect: During his exploration, John came across some of my banana trees. When he saw my people gathering from them, he quickly decided that I didn’t actually need to feed my people, and cut them down. About 10 minutes later, I was complaining to him about my lack of food, and how I couldn’t do the expansion I had wanted to do, which he was obviously very amused by, and so he told me what he had done. While I was understandably a little annoyed, I was also very pleased: When I think of strategy, using your Sawmill workers to cut down your opponents fruit trees to limit his expansion seems a lot more subtle and interesting than merely throwing increasing quantities of soldiers at him!

We’ll be very interested to hear what you think of the new dynamics, and maybe the multiplayer save will motivate some of you to give multiplayer a try, too!

John and I will finish revamping the tutorial (assuming we don’t go off on another tangent), and will upload a new patch on Monday or Tuesday.

Until next week!

notes.title: Weekly Update 8 - Fruit Gatherer
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/4aa0990cc9921823c6dfc231222b7cbddaaad8e0.png[/img]
[h1]Hi everyone,[/h1]
This past week has been spent with us focusing primarily on the gatherer and fruit tree dynamics. While John had already finished the tree by last week, the tree was not functional at the time of our post. As of now, the tree is functional. Players can harvest bananas themselves, the fruit regrows over time, and we have a functioning Gatherer’s Hut which collects the banana automatically. With this change, players will be able to gain much more food early on (compared to the Hunter’s Hut), which should speed up the early game a little and make it less repetitive. At the same time, the number of trees available to the players will stay limited throughout the game, making it a much less scalable option for food production in the mid and late game.

Developing the Gatherer and fruit tree mechanics have been an all-encompassing task in the past week, primarily because I wanted to take the time to improve my code. The mechanic is largely based on an existing mechanic used by the Sawmill (find trees, send a worker to them, collect resources, return to the building), but when I initially created the Sawmill, I expected for this mechanic to be used only by the Sawmill. As a result, the code was not sufficiently scalable and I decided to improve it to make it more flexible and robust. Consequently, it has distracted me a little from my work on the pirates, but I am very pleased with the current state of the mechanic, and I am expecting that any future bugs will be much easier to find and fix. As mentioned last week, we will also be using the same system for the Stonecutter, so the work needed to implement that is largely done already.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/51e85ae6851d3034122d07dd7d623b320b07e0ae.png[/img]
To round out the banana groves, we also added a smaller banana tree that won’t have fruit, but which adds some density to the banana areas. Finally, we also added a new function to the sawmill to enable/disable cutting of fruit trees by the Sawmill workers. The animations used for gathering are currently still the same as the ones for cutting down trees, but we are planning on overhauling animations more broadly once we replace the villager models with an updated version.

We will have to change the current tutorial a little to accommodate the replacement of the Hunter’s Hut, and will go through some more testing before I upload the new changes for everyone!

Until next week!

notes.title: Weekly Update 6 - Seed Inventory
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/7c480544aeab2c47181ce979aa58614b05ca0467.png[/img]
[h1]Hi everyone,[/h1]
First of all, happy Halloween! We unfortunately won't have any pumpkin themed changes in the game for the occasion, but you are always welcome to hunt for some of the scarier bugs to celebrate ;).

As I mentioned two weeks ago, a friend of mine has been pretty excited about contributing to the game and has been learning blender for a while. This past week, John taught him the basics of creating trees and plants, and we are excited to see how a second perspective on the plants will help with variety for new biomes and more engaging landscapes. As far as I understand, creating plants is a pretty difficult process, especially when trying to make them perform well, so it will likely be a few weeks or months before we see a payoff from this!

On my side, I have started working on improving the pirates, and so far, things are going quite well. In addition to what I mentioned last week, we have also been thinking about how to make pirates less of a jump scare. While I am currently working on the pirates investigating a threat when they initially hear it (to move around plants and trees toward the origin of a noise), this would still leave them being very silent, with the player potentially being unaware of being pursued. To change this, we are thinking of adding some sounds to the pirates themselves (rowdy behaviour, chants, shouts, or something similar). This will allow the player to hear them from further away, and potentially sneak around them when they are not ready to engage yet.

Finally, I have been working on some bugs (especially issues with Opal Reef), and I have also gotten around to creating a seed inventory in the book! The seed inventory will show you how many seeds you have purchased and how many are still available, and I have also updated some of the tooltips accordingly (the “not yet implemented” tooltip for the seeds was very confusing to many, as the seeds were working fine, but the tooltip itself had not been properly implemented yet).
I will upload the bug fixes and new seed inventory once I have fixed the last bugs on my list, before getting back to the pirates!

Until next week!

notes.title: Weekly update 5 - Settings menu and construction sites
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/0cf70b6e4c8a570ab84df1185882a3577f2002b3.png[/img]
[h1]Hi everyone,[/h1]
As always, thank you very much for all of your feedback! I have been a little out of touch with our social media last week, as I have finally taken a few days off at the start of the week (the last few months have been pretty crazy), but I trust that John was on top of things in my stead. Luckily, having some time off has really helped me to focus on coding, and I think we made pretty good progress as a result! 

The new settings menu (including key bindings) is finished, we finally have a button to return to the menu from the game, and John has created fencing/ropes around each building model. The last part is completely new (the final changes were made today), so I haven’t had a chance to implement this new system yet - I will work on it this weekend and upload all of the changes as soon as I finish it.

The new ropes are primarily to address peoples’ feedback telling us that it was difficult to know when you had selected blueprints (to add materials to the construction site or check on progress). When you place a building from now on, you should see the construction area fenced off with the ropes, and selecting the construction site will bring up the blueprint as usual. Once the construction is completely finished, the ropes will disappear (also addressing some older feedback that it was difficult to know when the buildings were completely built). Please let us know what you think of this new system, and if it makes selecting construction sites a little more intuitive than it used to be. If people like the system, we will upgrade the look of the ropes and construction site, potentially adding some crates and boxes to show how much of the construction materials are already on site. 

As I mentioned last week, I will be turning back to gameplay improvements after uploading the next update, especially pirates/combat. Even though it isn’t particularly apparent at this point, the game actually has a lot of mechanics for stealth and more interesting jungle combat in place already: 

Being close to trees/shrubbery gives players and soldiers a stealth bonus, making them more difficult to be detected; shooting a gun reduces any stealth bonus a player has; soldiers and pirates have 2 stages of awareness of each other/the player (one of being aware that someone is close, and one of actually having seen the opponent), etc. Unfortunately, using these systems to their full potential required more dynamic pirates and soldiers (who go to check when they “hear” an opponent in the jungle, then potentially lose track of the player and return to their position, etc.), and we had some issues with this when we first implemented it. Considering we had a lot on our plate at the time, we decided to keep pirates as a static challenge (aside from the pirate waves), and to add more important systems first. At this stage of the development, however, John and I both feel that improving the pirates is the right priority, and I will start working on them again as of this weekend!

Until next week!

notes.title: Weekly Update 3 - Changes to Opal Reef
notes.content:
[h1]Hi everyone,[/h1]
As usual, thank you very much for your feedback throughout the week! We have just uploaded the latest patch, which fixes some issues, and adds a new UI feature.

The new UI feature can be found just under the inventory in most buildings, and shows you which villagers are scheduled to interact with the building. This means you can now tell that someone is already on their way to bring wood to a construction site, or to pick up stone from a Quarry - which helps be a bit more aware of what is happening.

While we like the functionality, it does make some of the building book a little more cluttered than we’d like, so we have been thinking about moving this function to its own tab in the book, so you have a cleaner overview of the key functions of the building, and can get into the details only if you choose to. If we do this, we would probably also move the worker tabs to the same page to make room on the right of the building book. Let us know what you think about those ideas!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/a41ab58f06ee09c32a62e8d9395ba976322727fc.jpg[/img]
(The new outstanding tasks UI can seem a little cluttered at times)

We have also finally caught up with updating the port on Opal Reef, getting rid of the old “port” building (which, for the nostalgic of you was actually labelled "the courthouse’ and was the first model that John made for the game in Sketchup - back when this game design idea was very much being prototyped - and before he fell in love with Blender), and replacing it with the new one that was already in Spike Ridge. This has necessitated moving the port down to the waterfront, which changes the layouts of the starting areas and increases the distances from the warehouse to the port. 

As a result, the map feels quite different to Spike Ridge with its closer proximity between the two. We are happy with this for the moment though will consider making the path a little easier to connect the two if there is enough feedback for it. Warning: This change will actually break any games you previously saved on Opal Reef. If anyone wants to finish a game they saved on there, let me know and I will try to help.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/ffdd36abbc68e7361389bc6eab880c3841b2e321.jpg[/img]
(New position of the port in Opal Reef)

We have also had a lot of feedback telling us that the existing trailer and screenshot didn’t really reflect the depth of the game, and asking us to do a sort of “developer playthrough” to show how it can be played. While neither of us has ever done anything like this, we decided to give it a shot - which did not work out very well in our first try. The second time we already saw improvements, and the third time was pretty much spot on. So of course, I had forgotten to hit “record” on that one. 

That means we still have the sound but not the video, and while I would love to spare John having to record it with me again, the randomness of resources would make it rather strange to hear us talking about metal mines close-by when there aren’t any in the video. We will try to do our fourth take this weekend, and hopefully I will press record this time. (It is also amazing to me just how many things we have to do that aren’t actually game development at this stage.)

We will continue with bug fixing (at this point, it’s mostly elusive bugs, but some of which are pretty consistent), adding keybindings (being able to save settings has made this possible now), and I will be adding options for players to define their grid snap (how buildings align to others) and angle snap (how finely you can rotate buildings) - that way the city builders among us will have a few more options!

Until next week!

notes.content:
[h1]Hi everyone,[/h1]
Thank you for all of the bug reports and feedback this week, it is very much appreciated. We really appreciate that you have started using the steam forum for your reports, it makes things a lot easier for us, and allows everyone to track progress on bugs. 

Based on your feedback, we uploaded two patches this week, which again mostly focused on save files. We felt that it was really important to eliminate whatever bugs stopped you from continuing your games after you put hours into them, so this took priority in development. 

Another point of major comments has been feedback for the player. This ranges from getting more information on the output of buildings, over having more feedback to clicking buttons, to having a better sense of what direction your building is facing as you place it. 

As a result, the update last Saturday also included a new arrow when placing building blueprints, so you are able to tell which way the building is facing, and where your villagers will enter buildings. 

We have also created a new UI component which will tell you which villagers are on their way to or from a building:

At the moment, you are able to see most of the scheduled tasks, but it is not updating at quite the right times, and some of the tasks aren’t deleted until about a minute after the task is completed. Once I refine these issues, I will add it to the next update. Hopefully this will give you a better understanding of what is happening at any given time when you interact with the buildings.

Beyond that, we have also created a new system for tooltips:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/9cd4e765b86e89876462ab88adcc6204dcfa9a33.png[/img]
Again, the feature is already created, but we have not managed to implement the tooltips for too many of the UI elements yet. With this one, we are thinking of rolling the tooltips out as we go, so every update will likely include a few more tooltips than the previous.

Finally, I had promised a setting to rebind keys last week, and I have started on this as well. I am expecting that I will be able to make good progress on it this weekend, and if everything goes well, it should be included in the next update (likely early next week).

Until next week, and don’t hesitate to reach out to us with any questions or feedback!

notes.title: Weekly Update 1 - Welcome!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/cd760cd47358eba0d39b1951fd11e702e1d9f47c.png[/img]
[h1]Hi everyone, and welcome to Path to Prosperity![/h1]
First of all: Thank you all for your interest in the game! Getting the game to its current state has been a long and pretty exciting journey, so we are looking forward to sharing the next part of it with you.
Secondly, we wanted to take a moment to introduce ourselves as well as the game (though some of you already have 30+ hours in the game, so the latter part may be superfluous).

[h3]The team:[/h3]
The development team consists of primarily two of us (my name is Phil, I am the programmer, John is the artist), but we have a few friends who pitch in when they can. Both John and I are working on non-game related things in our “day jobs”, so we started development of Path to Prosperity because it was the game that we wanted to play and couldn’t find.

[h3]The game:[/h3]
That brings us to the game: We are big fans of strategy games, but we disliked the focus on reaction speed and predetermined build orders in many of them, as that doesn't seem very “strategic”. We thought for a long time about how we could improve on that, and our solution was to take away the player’s god-like (and almost all-knowing) top-down perspective. As with an old pre-satellite era commander, in our game, the player has to anticipate what will happen a lot more than react to what they can see is happening on their mini-map.

The game is currently pretty fun to play (we think so, and the time invested by quite a few of you seems to support that), but obviously there are a few bugs, UI issues, and we have many plans to expand on the features. 

You can find our current plans on the roadmap of the website: https://www.pathtoprosperitygame.com/roadmap.php

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38555898/7c95f1b462410771fb34206860c65e195a0d1df3.png[/img]

Considering we have a ton of ideas for new features, we really want to figure out what you, the players, want to get out of the game. Ideally, we’ll get around to implementing most of what’s on the roadmap, but we will prioritise based on what the community wants to see. Please join us on our discord https://discord.gg/33VxSnZ to discuss your thoughts (and report bugs). We will also start a discussion on the steam forum in case you prefer to comment there. Two of you have already started reporting bugs on there, and we appreciate you starting the conversation!

That brings us to these little updates. We really want there to be a discussion between players and us about what people enjoy about the game, how we can improve it, etc. We have multiple social media platforms for you to share your opinion with us, but it also has to be a two way street. As such, we will try to write a little update each week to describe what we have been up to, and what comes next.

[h3]The past week:[/h3]
As some of you have probably seen, we have already put out two hotfixes since release, and we are releasing another minor update tonight. You will be able to find any patch notes in the steam discussions forum, and we will try to also keep you updated here. Last week was mostly focused on a few save function issues, which had prevented games from saving and loading all data. Most of those should be fixed now, as far as we can tell (apparently a few more save bugs were created by my fixes, so I will address that ASAP).

[h3]The coming weeks:[/h3]
To start with, we want to also acknowledge that we haven't gotten around to all of your feedback from the past week yet. We are still working on it, and will keep releasing fixes as they come up. In particular, we found out that the lack of an option to change your key-bindings means that some regions with particular keyboard layouts can’t really play the game at the moment. I will prioritise getting that done.

John wants to improve the art overall in the long run, but he has decided to start the process by addressing earlier models that aren’t up to the same standards as the newer work. Specifically, he wants to start by modelling better Villagers and Pirates. He has already been working on improving some of the fundamentals, and from what I can tell, he has made some good improvements - they are not ready for this week's release, but will hopefully be upgraded next week. 

Please let us know if you have any thoughts on the game, balance, or have found bugs!

Until next week, and good luck finding the secrets of the island!
